post.caption: A platinum flute inspired Density 21.5. In 1896, William Haynes of Boston made America's first gold flute. In 1927, flutist Georges Barrère bought a gold Haynes flute. He played a gold flute for about ten years. In 1935, Haynes made him the first American platinum flute. It was ninety percent platinum and ten percent iridium. The composer Edgard Varèse wrote a solo piece for it. He named it Density 21.5, after platinum's density. Barrère premiered it at Carnegie Hall on February 16, 1936. A project called Density 2036 ends in 2036, a century later.
